description: Verify that DUT reassembles when the second fragment arrives within ipIniReassembleTimeout, but drops the bucket when the second fragment arrives AFTER the timer has expired — two-phase test of the reassembly timer
approach:
[Objective]
Validate the timer's gating effect: same fragment shape, two timing schedules. Phase A: late fragment arrives just under the timer — DUT must reassemble normally. Phase B: late fragment arrives just past the timer — DUT must have already dropped the bucket and ignore the late arrival.

[Scenario — chronological]
  Phase A:
    1. Tester → DUT: fragment 0 (MF=1)
    2. Tester → DUT: fragment 1 (MF=0) at delay < ipIniReassembleTimeout
    3. Observation: DUT → Tester Echo Reply with matching id/seq/data.

  Phase B:
    4. Tester → DUT: fragment 0 (MF=1) (new id)
    5. Tester → DUT: fragment 1 (MF=0) at delay > ipIniReassembleTimeout
    6. Observation: DUT → Tester nothing — bucket already dropped.

[Pass condition]
Phase A produces an Echo Reply with matching id/seq/data; Phase B produces no Reply.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_phase_a_echo_id / _seq / _data_mismatch — Phase A reply present but field wrong
• Fail_phase_a_no_reply — Phase A produced no reply (timer too short or reassembly broken)
• Fail_phase_b_replied — Phase B produced a reply despite the late fragment (timer not expiring)

verdicts.Pass: Phase A reassembled in time, Phase B dropped late — normal timer behaviour
verdicts.Fail_phase_a_no_reply: Phase A produced no reply — timer too aggressive or reassembly broken
verdicts.Fail_phase_b_replied: Phase B emitted a reply despite the late fragment — timer not expiring
